_comment: treg endpoint per capability, chosen in M1 (2026-10-29). Scrapers read IDs and caps only from here. max_cost_usd is sent as X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost on every call (treg's default is $1). Details: docs/endpoints.md

maps_search.price_type: per call with rows (empty reply free)
maps_search.note: Rows already include phone, website, hours, rating, place_id: no separate place-details call. limit>100 still returns 100, so 100 = saturated cell (M8).

serp.price_type: per call at limit 100 ($0.00015 per 10 results of depth)
serp.note: Rows: title, url, snippet, displayed_url, domain, position. Fallback discovery for people (X-ray); also company-name -> domain lookups.

web_extract.note: JS-site fallback for M4 only. output.pages[].markdown

people_search.price_type: per row returned (pagination.size is the price dial, max 200)
people_search.note: Primary people discovery. Use profileLocation (20/20 in-state); plain 'location' matched 13/20. Page with pagination.token from the previous response; tokens expire (a 6-day-old one returned 0 rows and total 0, no error). Rows carry profileUrl, lastJobTitle, address, lastCompanyName/Url/Website/Size/Industry, so no profile or company lookup is needed.

people_count.note: --dry-run: how many people match, before paying for rows. Same filter object as people_search. Response: total, success.

companies_count.note: --dry-run in company mode. Same filter object as companies_search. Response: total, success.

people_enrich.note: Only for profile URLs found via X-ray SERP. Returns name, title, company, location.

company_profile.note: Company mode. Test returned name, description, followers, employees, location but no website.

companies_search.price_type: per row returned (pagination.size is the price dial, max 200)
companies_search.note: Company mode (M12): discovery by keyword / location / industry / headcount, and --input URLs one by one via {companyId: {include: [url]}}. Chosen over treg.companies.search, which has no state or city filter. Rows: name, lid, urn, url, description, address ('[street,] [ZIP,] City, State, Country'), numberOfEmployees, headcountRange {gte, lte}, industry, foundedYear, type, website, slogan, specialties [{value}], pictureUrl, phone. 'SaaS' + 'Texas, United States' = 2,081 matches.

company_domain_from_linkedin.note: M10: email domain when a person row has the company's LinkedIn page but no website. Response: found, email_domain.

company_by_name.price_type: per hit; leadocean ($0, 93% hit) first, then blitzapi ($0.000495)
company_by_name.note: M10 last resort for a missing domain. Rows are provider-native; only a row whose name matches is used.

email_find_person.note: Tier 1 work email. Hit rate 15/30 (50%). Response: found, email, all_emails.

email_find_person_fallback.price_type: per hit, M11 average ($0.0048 quickenrich - $0.01 moltsets); misses free once orbisearch is excluded
email_find_person_fallback.note: Tier 2, only for tier-1 misses; tries quickenrich, trykitt, aiark, moltsets. Excluded: blitzapi (tier 1 already asked), enrow (async, slow), orbisearch (the only per-call provider under the cap: bills $0.0062 on every attempt for a treg-observed 1.6% hit rate; it was the whole cost of M1's billed misses), tomba (M11 run: 0 hits in 7 tries, up to 125 s each, 72% of the run's time; it pushed one call past the 180 s timeout, and the hit that came after was billed but never received). Never send X-Treg-Route-Verify here: it waterfalled 5 providers, ran >120 s and cost ~$0.018.

email_verify.price_type: per success (contactout free first, then orbisearch)

phone_find_person.price_type: per hit, M11 average (leadocean free, blitzapi $0.000495, quickenrich $0.0048); no provider bills misses

company_emails_by_domain.price_type: reserves one search credit (~$0.0245) per domain; free if no results
company_emails_by_domain.note: Opt-in M5 fallback (--paid-emails) for businesses whose website shows no email. Too expensive as a default. One credit covers up to 10 emails, so always ask for 10. Response: data.emails[] with value, type (generic/personal), confidence, position, verification.status.
